About the Thailand Lottery

The Thailand Lottery — officially the Thai Government Lottery (สลากกินแบ่งรัฐบาล) — is run by the Government Lottery Office (GLO) and drawn twice a month, normally on the 1st and 16th (occasionally shifted a day for public holidays). Draws start at around 2:30pm Thailand time and the full results are announced by late afternoon. The Thaiger publishes the winning numbers on this page minutes after each draw, with every past draw archived on its own results page — see the latest Thai lottery results for 01 August 2026.

Tickets are pre-printed with a six-digit number and cost 80 baht from licensed street vendors and official outlets nationwide. Anyone aged 20 or over can play — including foreigners, who can claim prizes with their passport and winning ticket.

How to check your Thai lottery ticket

  1. Find the six-digit number printed on your ticket.
  2. Use the lottery checker on this page — choose the draw date, enter your number and hit search — or compare it against the results above.
  3. Won? Claim at the GLO in Nonthaburi or an authorised agent within two years of the draw date (0.5% stamp duty applies to government lottery prizes).

Thailand Lottery FAQ

When is the next Thailand Lottery draw?

The Thailand Lottery is drawn on the 1st and 16th of every month (moved by a day or two when the date falls on certain public holidays). The draw starts at around 2:30pm Thailand time and results are published on this page the same afternoon.

What is the Thailand Lottery first prize?

The first prize is 6,000,000 baht per winning ticket. The two tickets numbered immediately above and below the first-prize number each win 100,000 baht.

How do I check my Thai lottery numbers?

Enter your six-digit ticket number in the lottery checker on this page and select the draw date, or open the results page for that draw. Every past draw has its own archived results page.

Can foreigners play the Thailand Lottery?

Yes. Foreigners can buy official 80-baht tickets from licensed vendors and claim prizes by presenting the winning ticket and their passport. A 0.5% stamp duty is deducted from government lottery prizes.

How long do I have to claim a Thai lottery prize?

Prizes must be claimed within two years of the draw date at the Government Lottery Office in Nonthaburi or an authorised agent.

Where do these Thailand Lottery results come from?

All results on this page come from the official Government Lottery Office (GLO) draw and are updated shortly after each draw is completed.
